Promote the Layers of an mcml to Networks

Source: R/mcml.R
as_tna.Rd

as_tna() turns an mcml object into a netobject_group: one network for the cluster-level (macro) layer, followed by one per cluster for the within-cluster layers. The stored weights are carried over as they are – nothing is re-normalised – so the networks hold the aggregation and type chosen when the mcml was built. Despite its name it returns Nestimate networks, not tna models; a tna model passed to it is returned unchanged.

This is the step that lets an MCML result reach the verbs that take a group of networks: printing, the network metrics of summary(), bootstrap_network() (for an mcml built from sequences, whose layers keep them; the layers of a cluster_summary() result carry none) and drawing with cograph.

Usage

as_tna(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'mcml'
as_tna(x, expand = NULL, ...)

# Default S3 method
as_tna(x, ...)

Arguments

x

An mcml object from cluster_summary() or build_mcml(). The default method also takes a tna model.

...

Not used.

expand

For the mcml method: clusters whose member states replace the collapsed cluster node in the macro network, as in macro_network(). Default NULL (the macro network stays fully collapsed). The within-cluster networks are not affected. It needs an mcml that build_mcml() built from a wide sequence frame, a sequence matrix or an event log; one from cluster_summary(), an edge list, a netobject or a tna model raises an error of class nestimate_no_expand_source.

Value

A netobject_group: a named list whose first element, macro, is the k x k cluster-level network, followed by one network per cluster. Print it for one row per layer (nodes, edges, weight range), call summary() for the network metrics of each layer, and draw a layer with cograph::splot(). Each element is a netobject (class c("netobject", "cograph_network")) with the layer's weights, initial probabilities, node and edge tables and data, and records method = "relative" when the mcml holds row-normalised weights (type = "tna"), method = "co_occurrence" for symmetrised counts (type = "cooccurrence"), and method = "frequency" for counts (type "raw" or "frequency") and for the aggregates of cluster_summary(). With expand, the macro element is the mixed-resolution network of macro_network() instead of the fully collapsed one. The default method returns a tna model unchanged and raises an error for any other class.

Details

Workflow


# Full MCML workflow
net <- build_network(data, method = "relative")
cs   <- cluster_summary(net, clusters = group_assignments)
nets <- as_tna(cs)

# Every layer is an ordinary netobject
print(nets)      # one line per layer
summary(nets)    # network metrics per layer

Sink nodes

Every cluster is returned, whatever its row sums. A node with no outgoing weight is a legitimate sink (a terminal state), and its row stays all zero in the network, for method = "relative" and "frequency" alike: the stored weights are never re-normalised, so a sink row needs no special handling.

See also

cluster_summary and build_mcml to create the input object, macro_network for a macro layer with one cluster expanded, as_networks for the psychometric-network counterpart

Examples

set.seed(1)
mat <- matrix(runif(36), 6, 6)
rownames(mat) <- colnames(mat) <- LETTERS[1:6]
clusters <- list(G1 = c("A", "B"), G2 = c("C", "D"), G3 = c("E", "F"))
cs <- cluster_summary(mat, clusters)
nets <- as_tna(cs)
nets
#> Group Networks (4 groups)
#> 
#>   Group  Nodes  Edges  Weights
#>   macro  3      9      [1.076, 2.706]
#>   G1     2      4      [0.266, 0.945]
#>   G2     2      4      [0.212, 0.935]
#>   G3     2      4      [0.340, 0.870]
summary(nets)
#> Network metrics by group:
#>                       metric  macro     G1      G2     G3
#>                   Node Count      3      2       2      2
#>                   Edge Count      9      4       4      4
#>              Network Density      1      1       1      1
#>                Mean Distance  1.863 0.6584  0.7162 0.5839
#>            Mean Out-Strength  6.181  1.122   1.207  1.353
#>              SD Out-Strength 0.5072 0.1253  0.7034 0.4867
#>             Mean In-Strength  6.181  1.122   1.207  1.353
#>               SD In-Strength 0.8432 0.6844 0.08534 0.2021
#>              Mean Out-Degree      3      2       2      2
#>                SD Out-Degree      0      0       0      0
#>  Centralization (Out-Degree)      0      0       0      0
#>   Centralization (In-Degree)      0      0       0      0
#>                  Reciprocity      1      1       1      1
